definitionEn: to throw away or get rid of something you no longer want or need
situation: You throw out an object, a draft or an idea because it is no longer useful to you.

examples.text: Before moving house, we [[discarded]] boxes of old magazines that nobody had opened in years.
The researchers [[discarded]] their first theory when new data failed to support it.
Staff must [[discard]] any food that has passed its use-by date.

texts: Halve the peppers and [[discard]] the seeds.
Good editors know when to [[discard]] a weak paragraph.
Never [[discard]] receipts until you have checked your bank statement.

badCollocation.noteRu: От приглашения или предложения отказываются — decline или turn down. Discard — выбросить ненужное или отбросить идею.

collocationTask.prompt: Peel the potatoes and ___ the skins.
collocationTask.explanationRu: Кожуру, упаковку и мусор выбрасывают — discard. Reject и dismiss — отклонить предложение или идею, abandon — бросить машину, дом или проект.

nuance.text: Once you have checked the contents, you can [[discard]] the plastic wrapping.
nuance.explanationRu: Discard — выбросить то, что у вас уже есть и больше не нужно. Reject — не принять то, что вам предлагают; к упаковке это не подходит.

reverse.text: She [[rejected]] the job offer because the salary was too low.
reverse.explanationRu: От предложения работы отказываются — reject или turn down. Discard — выбросить за ненадобностью, а не отклонить.

fixIt.text: Once the contracts had been scanned, we [[deleted]] all the paper copies.
fixIt.explanationRu: Delete — удалить файл или текст в компьютере. Бумажные копии выбрасывают — discard.

reply.context: A colleague messages: "We've got three pages of ideas from the brainstorm. Do we keep them all?"
options: Let's discard the meeting and brainstorm again next week.
Let's discard the weakest ones and focus on the two or three that could really work.
It is advisable that the aforementioned ideas be discarded forthwith.
reply.explanationRu: Идеи можно discard — отбросить как ненужные. Встречу не discard, а cancel или postpone. Третий вариант звучит как юридический документ, а не ответ коллеге.

rewrite.original: We threw away the old sofa because it was falling apart.
rewrite.frame: The old sofa ____ because it was falling apart.
rewrite.explanationRu: Нужен пассив: the sofa was discarded.

definitionEn: to officially allow a patient to leave hospital or a soldier to leave the army
senseNote: Здесь — выписать пациента или уволить со службы; значения «сбрасывать (отходы)» и «исполнять (обязанности)» не рассматриваются.
situation: Doctors decide a patient is well enough to go home, or the army lets a soldier leave.

examples.text: She was [[discharged]] from hospital two days after the operation and is now recovering at home.
After injuring his back in training, he was [[discharged]] from the navy and went back to university.
The ward is full because patients cannot be [[discharged]] until someone can care for them at home.

texts: Grandad was [[discharged]] on Friday and is already bored at home.
She was [[discharged]] from the army after twelve years of service.
Most patients are [[discharged]] within a week of surgery.

badCollocation.noteRu: Из гостиницы «выписываются» сами — check out. Discharge — выписка из больницы или увольнение с военной службы.

collocationTask.explanationRu: Пациента выписывают — discharge. Fire — уволить работника, expel — исключить из школы, resign — уйти с должности самому.

nuance.text: The hospital will [[discharge]] him as soon as his temperature is back to normal.
nuance.explanationRu: Discharge — официально отпустить пациента домой. Dismiss — уволить работника или отвергнуть идею; пациента так не «выписывают».

reverse.text: The company [[dismissed]] two managers after the audit.
reverse.explanationRu: Уволить сотрудника компании — dismiss. Discharge в этом значении используют для больницы и военной службы.

fixIt.text: The doctor said she would [[write out]] my father on Friday if his tests were normal.
fixIt.explanationRu: Write out — выписать рецепт или чек. Пациента из больницы «выписывают» — discharge.

reply.context: A friend texts: "Any news about your grandmother? Is she still in hospital?"
options: Yes, she discharged the doctors this morning and went home.
Affirmative. The patient's discharge has been duly processed.
Good news, they discharged her this morning, so she's back home now.
reply.explanationRu: Выписывают пациента (discharged her), а не врачей. Второй вариант звучит как больничный отчёт, а не сообщение другу.

definitionEn: to make information known, especially something that was secret or private
situation: A company, official or person reveals information that was private or secret until then.

examples.text: The company refused to [[disclose]] the price it had paid for the land.
You are not legally required to [[disclose]] a medical condition to your employer.
Police have not [[disclosed]] the identity of the man who was arrested.

texts: Doctors cannot [[disclose]] your records without your consent.
The buyer asked us not to [[disclose]] the price.
You must [[disclose]] any previous convictions on the form.

badCollocation.noteRu: «Раскрыть дело» — solve a case. Disclose — сделать известной скрытую информацию, а не найти преступника.

collocationTask.prompt: refuse to ___ the identity of the buyer
collocationTask.explanationRu: Disclose — сообщить то, что знаешь сам. Discover и uncover — узнать или обнаружить скрытое, disclaim — отказаться от ответственности.

nuance.text: The bank must [[disclose]] all its fees before you sign the contract.
nuance.explanationRu: Disclose — сообщить другим то, что знаешь. Discover — самому узнать что-то новое; банк не «обнаруживает» свои комиссии, а раскрывает их клиенту.

reverse.text: Scientists have [[discovered]] a new species of frog in the rainforest.
reverse.explanationRu: Найти что-то новое — discover. Disclose — раскрыть сведения, которые у вас уже есть.

fixIt.text: Neither company is allowed to [[open]] the details of the deal to journalists.
fixIt.explanationRu: «Раскрыть» сведения — не open, а disclose (или reveal). Open — открыть дверь, файл или счёт.

reply.context: A friend asks: "So how much did they offer you? Come on, tell me!"
options: Sorry, I promised not to disclose the figure until I've signed the contract.
Let me disclose the envelope first, then I'll tell you.
Pursuant to the confidentiality clause, I am unable to disclose said figure.
reply.explanationRu: Disclose — сообщить скрытую информацию (сумму, условия). Конверт не disclose, а open. Третий вариант звучит как юридический документ, а не ответ другу.

rewrite.original: The hospital did not reveal the patient's name.
rewrite.frame: The patient's name ____ by the hospital.
rewrite.explanationRu: Нужен пассив: the name was not disclosed.

definitionEn: the act of making secret or private information known to others
situation: Information that was kept secret or private is officially made public or shared with others.

examples.text: New rules require full [[disclosure]] of executives' pay in the annual report.
Data protection law restricts the [[disclosure]] of customers' personal details to third parties.
Her memoir includes the painful [[disclosure]] that she had struggled with gambling for years.

texts: The [[disclosure]] of the minister's private emails caused a scandal.
Full [[disclosure]]: I used to work for the company I'm reviewing.
Any [[disclosure]] of patient records requires written consent.

badCollocation.noteRu: «Раскрыть потенциал» — realise или fulfil your potential. Disclosure — только обнародование скрытых сведений.

collocationTask.prompt: full ___ of all fees and charges
collocationTask.explanationRu: Обязательное раскрытие информации — full disclosure. Exposure — разоблачение чего-то плохого, opening — открытие, appearance — появление.

nuance.text: Companies must make a formal [[disclosure]] of any risks to their investors.
nuance.explanationRu: Disclosure — официальное раскрытие сведений по закону или правилам. Revelation — неожиданное, сенсационное открытие; для отчёта инвесторам не подходит.

reverse.text: Her talent for comedy was a [[revelation]] to the audience.
reverse.explanationRu: Неожиданное приятное открытие — a revelation. Disclosure — официальное раскрытие информации, к таланту не подходит.

fixIt.text: Shareholders demanded the [[opening]] of the directors' salaries.
fixIt.explanationRu: «Раскрытие» сведений — disclosure. Opening — открытие магазина, выставки или счёта.

wordFormation.text: The [[disclosure]] of the documents led to a public inquiry.

definitionEn: the way a subject is discussed in public, in speech and writing
situation: You describe how politicians, the media and ordinary people talk and write about an issue.

examples.text: Many people feel that political [[discourse]] has become angrier since the rise of social media.
The course examines how gender is represented in academic and media [[discourse]].
Experts are calling for a calmer, better-informed public [[discourse]] on artificial intelligence.

texts: Online [[discourse]] often rewards outrage more than careful thought.
The scandal dominated political [[discourse]] for weeks.
Her book changed the [[discourse]] around mental health.

badCollocation.text: a [[discourse]] with a friend about films
badCollocation.noteRu: Дружеская беседа — conversation или chat. Discourse — книжное слово о том, как тема обсуждается в обществе или науке.

collocationTask.explanationRu: С discourse говорят engage in — «участвовать в обсуждении». Make, perform и conduct с этим существительным не сочетаются.

nuance.text: The study looks at how climate change is framed in political [[discourse]].
nuance.explanationRu: Discourse — вся совокупность того, как о теме говорят и пишут в обществе. Discussion — конкретное обсуждение между людьми; framed in political discussion звучит неестественно.

reverse.text: We had a long [[discussion]] about where to go on holiday.
reverse.explanationRu: Разговор нескольких людей о конкретном деле — discussion. Discourse — книжное слово для публичного обсуждения, а не беседы о поездке.

fixIt.text: Her thesis analyses how older people are portrayed in advertising and newspaper [[speech]].
fixIt.explanationRu: «Газетная речь» — не newspaper speech, а newspaper discourse (или language). Speech — устная речь или выступление.

definitionEn: the freedom or authority to decide what should be done in a particular situation
senseNote: Здесь — «усмотрение, право решать»; значение «тактичность, умение хранить тайну» не рассматривается.
situation: A manager, judge or official is allowed to decide for themselves how to act.

examples.text: Bonuses are paid at the [[discretion]] of the board, so they are never guaranteed.
The law gives judges wide [[discretion]] over the length of a sentence.
The hotel manager used her [[discretion]] and let us check out late at no extra cost.

texts: Leaving a tip is entirely at your [[discretion]].
Refunds are given at the manager's [[discretion]].
Parents should use their [[discretion]] about screen time.

badCollocation.noteRu: Правильный предлог — at: at your discretion («на ваше усмотрение»). On your discretion — калька с русского «на».

collocationTask.explanationRu: Говорят use (или exercise) your discretion — «действовать по своему усмотрению». Make, take и do с discretion не сочетаются.

nuance.text: Late essays are accepted only at the [[discretion]] of the course leader.
nuance.explanationRu: At the discretion of — «на усмотрение»: человек сам решает, как поступить. Decision — конкретное решение; сочетания at the decision of в английском нет.

reverse.text: The committee will make its final [[decision]] next week.
reverse.explanationRu: Решение принимают — make a decision. Discretion — не само решение, а право решать.

fixIt.text: Additional days off may be granted at the manager's [[choice]].
fixIt.explanationRu: «На усмотрение руководителя» — at the manager's discretion. Сочетание at someone's choice в английском не используется.

wordFormation.text: Staff may receive a [[discretionary]] bonus at the end of the year.

reply.context: A new colleague asks you: "Can I work from home on Fridays, or is there a strict rule?"
options: There's no strict rule. It's at your manager's discretion, so just ask her.
Working from home is a discretion, so you'll need to fill in a form.
Such matters fall within the discretionary purview of line management.
reply.explanationRu: At your manager's discretion — «на усмотрение руководителя». Discretion — не документ и не льгота. Третий вариант звучит как юридический текст, а не ответ коллеге.

rewrite.original: The manager decides whether customers get a refund.

definitionEn: unfair treatment of a person or group because of their race, sex, age or religion
senseNote: Выбрано основное значение — несправедливое отношение; редкое книжное значение «разборчивость, умение различать» не рассматривается.
situation: People are treated worse than others because of who they are, for example their age or gender.

examples.text: The company was fined for age [[discrimination]] after rejecting every applicant over fifty.
She believes she faced [[discrimination]] at work because she was pregnant.
Laws against [[discrimination]] on the grounds of disability were introduced in 1995.

texts: Racial [[discrimination]] is illegal in housing and employment.
Many older workers report [[discrimination]] when applying for jobs.
The charity offers free legal advice to victims of [[discrimination]].

badCollocation.noteRu: После discrimination нужен предлог against: discrimination against women. «Дискриминация женщин» с of — калька с русского.

collocationTask.explanationRu: Правильно discrimination against someone. Of — калька с русского «дискриминация кого-то», for и over здесь не употребляются.

nuance.text: The court ruled that paying women less for the same job was unlawful [[discrimination]].
nuance.explanationRu: Discrimination — несправедливые действия (платить меньше, не брать на работу). Prejudice — предубеждение в голове; незаконным может быть только поведение.

reverse.text: He admitted he had a [[prejudice]] against people with tattoos.
reverse.explanationRu: Предубеждение, мнение о людях — a prejudice against. Discrimination — это поступки, и «had a discrimination» не говорят.

fixIt.text: Older applicants often face [[discriminating]] when they look for work.
fixIt.explanationRu: После face нужно существительное: face discrimination. Discriminating — прилагательное «разборчивый» или форма глагола.

wordFormation.text: Campaigners say the new rules could lead to [[discrimination]] against part-time staff.

reply.context: A friend says: "My landlord won't rent his flats to families with kids. Is that even allowed?"
options: Well, it's his discrimination, so he can choose any tenants he likes.
I doubt it's legal. It sounds like discrimination against families.
One would posit that such conduct constitutes a discriminatory practice.
reply.explanationRu: Discrimination against families — несправедливое отношение к семьям с детьми. В первом ответе слово понято как «право выбора», а третий звучит как научная статья, а не ответ другу.

definitionEn: very bad or unsuccessful, in a way that is disappointing and depressing
senseNote: Здесь — «провальный, плачевный» (о результатах); значение «мрачный, унылый» (dismal weather) не рассматривается.
situation: Results, sales or a performance turn out much worse than expected, and everyone is disappointed.

examples.text: The team's [[dismal]] performance, with ten defeats in a row, cost the coach his job.
Sales of the new phone were so [[dismal]] that it was withdrawn after six months.
Despite a [[dismal]] start to the term, she worked hard and passed all her exams.

texts: The film was a [[dismal]] failure at the box office.
Voter turnout was [[dismal]] in the local elections.
The company blamed the weak economy for its [[dismal]] profits.

badCollocation.noteRu: Об ошибке говорят terrible, serious или grave mistake. Dismal — о результатах, продажах или выступлении: a dismal performance.

collocationTask.explanationRu: Устойчивое сочетание — a dismal failure («полный провал»). Gloomy, mournful и dark описывают настроение или атмосферу, а не неудачу.

nuance.text: The firm reported [[dismal]] sales for the third quarter in a row.
nuance.explanationRu: Dismal — об очень плохих результатах (продажах, оценках, выступлении). Gloomy — о мрачном настроении, погоде или прогнозе; gloomy sales не говорят.

reverse.text: Economists are [[gloomy]] about the country's prospects.
reverse.explanationRu: Gloomy about — пессимистично настроенный (о людях). Dismal описывает сами результаты, а не отношение людей к ним.

fixIt.text: Investors were worried by the company's [[dark]] sales figures for the winter.
fixIt.explanationRu: «Мрачные цифры» — не dark figures, а dismal (плачевные). Dark о результатах не говорят.

wordFormation.text: The first attempt to launch the service failed [[dismally]].

reply.context: A colleague asks: "How did the product launch go? I heard the numbers are in."
options: Great! Sales were dismal, so we're celebrating tonight.
The sales outcome may be characterised as dismal in nature, regrettably.
Not great, to be honest. The first-week sales were pretty dismal.
reply.explanationRu: Dismal — «плачевный, провальный», так что праздновать нечего. Второй вариант звучит неестественно и слишком официально для разговора с коллегой.

rewrite.original: The film did extremely badly at the box office.
rewrite.frame: The film was ____ at the box office.

definitionEn: a worried, sad feeling you get when something unpleasant and unexpected happens
situation: You feel shocked and disappointed after unexpected bad news, for example about a job or a plan.

examples.text: To her [[dismay]], the train was cancelled and she missed the interview.
Staff heard with [[dismay]] that the office would close and many would lose their jobs.
Much to the [[dismay]] of fans, the band cancelled its farewell tour.

texts: She looked at the bill in [[dismay]].
The decision caused widespread [[dismay]] among teachers.
Critics expressed [[dismay]] at the museum's decision to close early.

badCollocation.noteRu: «Впасть в уныние» — fall into despair; с dismay так не говорят. Обычно be dismayed или react with dismay.

collocationTask.explanationRu: Чувства «выражают» — express dismay, express concern. Say, tell и speak с существительным dismay не сочетаются.

nuance.text: To our [[dismay]], smoke started pouring out of the engine.
nuance.explanationRu: Dismay — тревога и смятение от неприятной неожиданности. Disappointment — огорчение, когда не оправдались ожидания; для дыма из двигателя это слишком слабое слово.

reverse.text: The film was a [[disappointment]] after all the good reviews.
reverse.explanationRu: Фильм, который не оправдал ожиданий, — a disappointment. Dismay — чувство, а не событие; «a dismay» не говорят.

fixIt.text: Much to our [[disturbance]], the concert was called off at the last minute.
fixIt.explanationRu: «К нашему огорчению» — to our dismay (или disappointment). Disturbance — шум, беспорядок или помеха, а не чувство.

wordFormation.text: Many parents were [[dismayed]] by the sudden rise in school fees.

reply.context: A friend texts: "How did your sister react to her new haircut?"
options: She stared at the mirror in total dismay. It was much shorter than she'd asked for.
She was full of dismay, so she gave the hairdresser a huge tip.
She expressed her profound dismay regarding the aforementioned haircut.
reply.explanationRu: In dismay — в смятении и огорчении, поэтому щедрые чаевые звучат нелогично. Третий вариант слишком официальный для переписки с другом.

rewrite.original: We were upset to find that the museum was closed.

definitionEn: the act of officially removing someone from their job
senseNote: Здесь — увольнение с работы; значения «пренебрежение (к идее)» и «отклонение (иска)» не рассматриваются.
situation: An employer officially tells a worker that they no longer have a job there.

examples.text: He took the company to court, claiming his [[dismissal]] had been unfair.
Stealing from the till is gross misconduct and can lead to instant [[dismissal]].
The union is fighting the [[dismissal]] of forty nurses at the city hospital.

texts: She is suing her former employer for unfair [[dismissal]].
The coach's [[dismissal]] came after five straight defeats.
Workers must receive written notice before [[dismissal]].

badCollocation.noteRu: Заявление об уходе по своему желанию — a resignation letter (hand in your resignation). Dismissal — увольнение по решению работодателя.

collocationTask.explanationRu: Юридический термин — unfair dismissal («незаконное увольнение»). Resignation — уход по своему желанию, retirement — выход на пенсию, release — освобождение.

nuance.text: He was shocked by his [[dismissal]], as nobody had ever complained about his work.
nuance.explanationRu: Dismissal — увольнение по решению работодателя. Resignation — уход по собственному желанию; собственный уход вряд ли шокирует человека.

reverse.text: She handed in her [[resignation]] to spend more time with her children.
reverse.explanationRu: Заявление об уходе подают сами — hand in your resignation. Dismissal — решение работодателя, его не «подают».

fixIt.text: After the scandal, the board announced the [[release]] of two senior managers.
fixIt.explanationRu: «Освобождение от должности» — dismissal. Release — освобождение из тюрьмы или выпуск фильма, продукта.

wordFormation.text: The [[dismissal]] of the head teacher divided the local community.

reply.context: At lunch, a colleague whispers: "Did you hear Mark was caught selling client data?"
options: Seriously? I hope he gets a dismissal and a pay rise.
Seriously? That's grounds for instant dismissal. I can't believe he'd risk it.
Indeed, one anticipates that his dismissal shall be effected forthwith.
reply.explanationRu: Grounds for dismissal — основание для увольнения. Увольнение и повышение зарплаты не сочетаются по смыслу, а третий вариант слишком официальный для разговора за обедом.

rewrite.original: She was fired unfairly, so she is taking her employer to court.
rewrite.frame: She is taking her employer to court for ____.
